note: Counts in entries are as of the entry date.

entries.summary: Imported 108 principles in 9 categories and 41 source repos from the initial research. No merges, no drops. Source repos are not pinned yet.
entries.reason: Starting point for the repo.

entries.summary: Checked the licence of all 41 source repos and recorded it in data/sources.json. 25 MIT, 6 Apache-2.0, 1 CC0-1.0, 1 CC-BY-SA-4.0, 3 no licence file found, 5 described by licence file. Pins still unset.
entries.reason: Licences must be known before any content is borrowed.

entries.summary: Merged 4.4 into 4.1. 4.4 is now an alias of 4.1; sources combined and wording folded into 4.1.
entries.reason: One test per cycle is a rule within red-green TDD.

entries.summary: Merged 4.5 into 5.3. 4.5 is now an alias of 5.3; sources combined and wording folded into 5.3.
entries.reason: The reproducing test is the first step of 5.3.

entries.summary: Merged 9.4 into 5.1. 9.4 is now an alias of 5.1; sources combined and wording folded into 5.1.
entries.reason: Same technique, same source (the Superpowers debugging skill).

entries.summary: Merged 5.6 into 5.10. 5.6 is now an alias of 5.10; sources combined and wording folded into 5.10.
entries.reason: Same rule.

entries.summary: Merged 2.11 into 6.3. 2.11 is now an alias of 6.3; sources combined and wording folded into 6.3.
entries.reason: Same rule.

entries.summary: Sharpened the wording of eight overlapping pairs (2.14/3.5, 7.6/7.10, 7.1/8.7, 4.9/7.12, 3.14/5.4, 8.5/9.9, 8.1/8.3, 2.5/3.1) and added a distinct_from note to each principle.
entries.reason: Each principle in a pair should have its own job and trigger.

entries.summary: principles schema 1.0.0 to 1.1.0: added optional aliases and distinct_from. Existing data stays valid; set schema_version to 1.1.0.
entries.reason: Merged IDs need to keep resolving, and overlapping principles need a note on how they differ.

entries.summary: Added 103 skills (one per principle, each with SKILL.md and SOURCES.md) and the data files for the skill map, taxonomy, source mapping, licences and scorecard, each with a schema.
entries.reason: One amalgamated skill per principle, built from the pinned sources.

entries.summary: Added four MIT source repos (41 to 45), pinned, for the 7.12 skill.
entries.reason: rstack's before-and-after is PolyForm Shield (link only), so 7.12 is built from MIT sources.

entries.summary: Rewrote run_order in data/taxonomy.json to describe the real slot order: Agent operations first, then test apps A, B and C, with Learn on the first run (slots 33-43). No slot was renumbered.
entries.reason: The old text described an order the slots no longer follow.

entries.summary: Added 19 agents (the coordinator, and a producer and reviewer for each of the nine phases) and 7 commands, generated by scripts/build-agents.py from the skill map, taxonomy, principles and skills. Each lists its skills by ID.
entries.reason: Agents and commands load the skills the map assigns to their phase, so they cannot drift from it.

entries.summary: sources schema 1.0.0: added optional commit_date and pin_source fields to repo entries. Existing entries stay valid.
entries.reason: Track the commit date and whether each pin came from the review record or default-branch HEAD.

entries.summary: Pinned all 45 source repos in data/sources.json to the commit they were reviewed at (pin_source review-record on all 45, none on github-head): 36 from data/licences.json and 9 from the review commits supplied with the Step 4 review (6 already matched, 3 re-pinned from default-branch HEAD). Added commit_date and pin_source across all 45 repos.
entries.reason: Every source repo now has a reproducible pinned commit.

entries.summary: Fixed test-plan path from ../../scorecard.csv to ../../data/scorecard.json across all 103 skills, updated skill 8.5 count from 108 to 103, gave reviewer agents a tools list (Bash for build, verify, debug, secure and review-and-ship; a prompt rule, not enforcement, because Cursor subagents ignore tools:), and wired NVIDIA SkillSpector 2.13.7 scanning of skills/ into CI with per-finding exceptions (rule, file, text, source line and a per-file cap).
entries.reason: Keep skills/, agents/ and CI checks accurate and aligned with the repository layout.

entries.summary: Added four developer guides in guides/developer/ (Developer Guide, Principles for Building Quality Software and Apps, Using the agents and commands, Testing the skills) and replaced the stub index. Published by scripts/build-site.py, which now rewrites guide links to files under docs/ as site-relative links, gives guide headings GitHub-style ids, orders the guides listing by the index, and fails on cursor.com/canvas links in a guide. Counts, aliases, the run order and the scorecard follow data/principles.json, data/taxonomy.json, data/skill-principle-map.json and data/scorecard.json; no principle, skill or source changed.
entries.reason: Publish the plain-language guides the site and README promised.

entries.summary: taxonomy.schema.json 2.0.0 drops test_apps[].skills; skill-principle-map.schema.json 2.0.0 drops clean_sources and link_only_sources; scorecard.schema.json 1.1.0 drops the fixed maximum on total; all three accept any single capital letter or All as a test app; changelog.schema.json 1.1.0 adds an optional top-level note. scripts/validate-data.py checks that each scorecard run's total is the sum of its scores.
entries.reason: Stored counts and fixed totals go stale as skills, sources and criteria change.

entries.summary: Removed hard-coded collection counts from the generated site and agent files (via scripts/build-site.py and scripts/build-agents.py), the READMEs, ATTRIBUTIONS.md, CREDITS.md, the skills (front matter source counts, 'of N' slots, skill 8.5's total) and the developer guides; reworded the taxonomy run_order and the sources research_run description without counts; verdict rules now use a share of the maximum score. NOTICE.md says all 45 source repos were checked.
entries.reason: Counts written into prose go stale whenever a principle, skill or source is added, merged or dropped.

entries.summary: Marked the project as alpha. README.md has a status badge and a warning under the title (title now 'AI SDLC Loop'). Every generated site page now has a fixed corner ALPHA ribbon (markup in the page wrapper of scripts/build-site.py, styles in docs/assets/style.css) and a visually hidden sentence for screen readers. The five merged-ID redirect pages are unchanged.
entries.reason: The project is a work in progress and has not been fully tested yet.

entries.summary: Added data/agent-contract.json (schema 1.0.0, with data/schemas/agent-contract.schema.json): the required output field assumptions_and_open_questions for every agent and the append-only JSON Lines format of the shared surface register. scripts/build-agents.py renders the field and the coordinator's register-as-inbox rules into agents/ and commands/, every command takes --register <path> (default .ai-sdlc/register.jsonl), and build-agents --check and check-skills fail if an agent lacks the field. Added scripts/register.py. Documented in agents/README.md, the Using the agents and commands guide and the agents page. No existing schema changed, so no existing schema_version moved.
entries.reason: Agents cannot ask the human mid-cycle, so their assumptions and open questions need a required, visible place that the coordinator and the human can both read.

entries.summary: Replaced the JSON-lines register request with one register-request block for assumptions, open questions and blockers: === REGISTER REQUESTS ===, [TYPE: statement] lines (types come from register.types in data/agent-contract.json, so a new type is a data change only), === END REGISTER REQUESTS ===. blocker is a new register type; impact and urgency are optional on entries and the coordinator rates them; entries gain an optional via field. agent-contract.schema.json and data/agent-contract.json move to 1.1.0. Every agent definition carries the instruction for agents that cannot write to the register, and build-agents --check and check-skills fail without the field, the block or the instruction. scripts/register.py ingest parses the block and writes statements verbatim; register.py selftest (run by build-agents --check) round-trips every type. Skill 1.1 now uses the block and carries the instruction.
entries.reason: Agents with no shell cannot write the register, so every agent needs one format that the coordinator can mirror verbatim, and a way to declare blockers.

entries.summary: Added planning-discipline wording to skills 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.6 and 1.7: locked decisions that downstream agents may not silently override (with a reviewer check), an exit test as reviewer checks for 1.2 and 1.4, an interview protocol for 1.4 (ground first, infer from the goal, one layer at a time by coupling, standard question format with the recommendation first), a decision sheet recorded in the spec, numbered Given/When/Then acceptance criteria with checks that name the criterion they prove, and rules against anchoring on the first option and against applying a preference or default silently (declare it as an assumption). Regenerated agents, commands and site; added a Planning discipline section to the Using the agents and commands guide. Principles, principle statements and the register-request block are unchanged.
entries.reason: Planning decisions the human has already made were open to silent reopening, and open choices could reach the build; these rules make decisions explicit, durable and checkable.

entries.summary: Added data/harnesses.json (schema data/schemas/harnesses.schema.json) and scripts/install-harness.py. scripts/new-project.sh --harness <name> now installs the skills, agents and loop commands into a new project in the project-level layout of Cursor, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi or GitHub Copilot in VS Code. The default, none, keeps the old behaviour. Paths must stay inside the project, and nothing is written to a harness's user or global settings. Loop commands carry an sdlc- prefix. Installed copies are MIT, like template/, except files adapted from share-alike sources (found from the per-source licences in data/licences.json), which keep CC BY-SA 4.0 and carry a NOTICE.md and the licence text in their own skill folder. Each file has a provenance comment stating its licence, and each SOURCES.md carries the copyright lines and licence links of its MIT and Apache sources. The project root holds only the template's MIT LICENSE. Added scripts/check-new-project.py to CI, which also asserts the licence of every installed file. Added the Use page (guides/use.md, published as docs/use.html), the last site nav item before the GitHub link, whose harness table and sections build-site.py generates from data/harnesses.json. Updated the README start section, the licence section and the folder READMEs.
entries.reason: Starting a project in a given harness meant copying and adapting the agent, command and skill files by hand. Keeping each harness's layout as data, generated from the same sources, lets every harness get the same loop without a second copy to maintain.

entries.summary: Added scripts/bootstrap.sh, a one-command Bootstrap for Cursor for solo developers and non-coders, run from inside a checkout. It asks where to put the project (home, Documents if it exists, or the folder next to the checkout) and what to call it, never inside the checkout, then runs new-project.sh for the solo profile and the Cursor harness, adds START-HERE.md and an always-on rule from the new template/bootstrap/ folder with a first-time note also at the top of the project's AGENTS.md, and runs a local git init on main, leaving the first commit to the agent. No GitHub, no accounts, no remote. It checks for git and python3 and does not install them; AI_SDLC_BOOTSTRAP_LOCATION and AI_SDLC_BOOTSTRAP_NAME skip the questions. new-project.sh now leaves template/bootstrap/ out of new projects. Added scripts/check-bootstrap.py to CI (fake home, copy of the checkout without .git as curl gives). Added a Bootstrap for Cursor section to the Use page, opening with why Bootstrap exists (hand the person to a Cursor agent that can handhold them), then requirements, a curl download or manual clone, and the questions; updated the README, scripts/README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the landing page.
entries.reason: Solo developers and non-coders need a start that does not mean choosing a profile, a harness and a target path by hand, or knowing what to say to the agent first. Teams keep new-project.sh.

entries.summary: README.md links the learning site (https://mitulamin.github.io/ai-sdlc-loop/) just after the introduction. The Use page link later in the README stays. The alpha status badge, warning and title are unchanged. The site is generated independently of the README, so docs/ is unchanged.
entries.reason: The GitHub Pages site was only linked from the Use page, deep in the README.

entries.summary: Extended the SkillSpector CI scan from skills/ to agents/, commands/, template/ and a throwaway install for each harness, and added the scan with the LLM analyzers on (scripts/skillspector-llm-scan.py, which uses xAI when XAI_API_KEY is set and otherwise NVIDIA Build with NVIDIA_INFERENCE_KEY and a pinned model, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b, because SkillSpector's own default for NVIDIA Build no longer answers; with backoff on failed calls), run by workflow skillspector-llm.yml on release-candidate tags (vX.Y.Z-rcN on a main commit) as groups derived from the repo, one skill family or folder per job, one after another, with a summary job that passes only when every group passed. The release tag vX.Y.Z and GitHub release follow only after that, on the same commit (RELEASING.md, workflow release-gate.yml, per-finding record). Reworded the reviewer agents' loads label in scripts/build-agents.py so SkillSpector's static parser can read every reviewer file.
entries.reason: The static scan covered only skills, but agents, commands, the template and the installed harness files are what an agent actually reads. A model-assisted pass catches intent that static rules miss, but it is slow, limited by provider rate limits and needs a person to triage its findings, so it runs per release candidate in small serial groups that can be re-run one at a time, and gates the release rather than every pull request.

entries.summary: principles schema 1.1.0 to 1.2.0: added optional related_practices (name, guide section, see_also principle ids). Existing data stays valid; set schema_version to 1.2.0.
entries.reason: Established practices that are not principles here need one recorded home in a skill, so the skill text, the agents and the principle pages can be checked against the data.

entries.summary: Every skill gained a Self-check section: questions the producer answers yes, no or N/A with evidence before handing off. Producers load it and end their report with a Principle self-check table; reviewers treat that table as a claim to test, and a report without it is a P1 finding; the coordinator puts its own table in run-summary.md. Practices described in the developer guides but not in the catalogue became related practices of the skill they fit, each with a Related practices entry, a self-check item and a reviewer check: the SOLID principles (single responsibility and loose coupling with 2.1, Liskov substitution and interface segregation with 2.2, dependency inversion, the twelve-factor app and acyclic dependencies with 2.3, open-closed with 2.5 as its YAGNI brake), composition over inheritance (2.5), the Unix philosophy (2.4), design by contract (2.9), strangler fig (2.12), convention over configuration and secure by default (2.14), least astonishment (3.6), the Boy Scout rule kept inside 3.2's scope (3.10), DRY with the rule of three and the Law of Demeter (3.11, keeping 2.5's duplicate-twice brake), fail fast (3.13), Gall's law (3.14), Goodhart's law (4.6), defence in depth (6.1), least privilege (6.2) and the robustness principle, strict at trust boundaries (6.3). scripts/check-skills.py and scripts/build-agents.py --check fail if a skill lacks its Self-check or its practices drift from data/principles.json. Principle pages list their related practices, and the developer guides link each practice to its skill. Principle statements are unchanged.
entries.reason: The skills told agents what to do but gave them no step to check their own work against it before handing off, and well-known practices such as SOLID and DRY lived only in the guides, where no agent reads them.
